method: NAIVE. Written straight from the deposited text using only the writing-l4-rules skill. No pipeline, no coverage table, no probe record, no independent test pass, no human gate. One pass, no review.
edition_encoded: Protection from Harassment Act 2014 (Singapore), 2020 Revised Edition, informal consolidation in force from 17 August 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/PHA2014.txt. The deposit carries the Act 23 of 2025 amendments with effect from 29 June 2026.

checks.command: l4 run pha-cases.l4 ; l4 run pha-civil-cases.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. One assertion records a DISAGREEMENT between the encoding and Illustration (b) to s 3 - see NOTES.md.

scope: Part 2 in full (ss 2 to 10: the five offences, the three enhanced-penalty provisions, and the offence of breaching an order) and Part 3 DIVISION 1 (ss 11, 11A, 12, 13, 13B and 14: the statutory tort, enhanced damages for online activity, the protection order, the expedited protection order, the mandatory treatment order, and the abolition of the common law tort). NOT ENCODED: s 9 (community order), the whole of Part 3 Division 2 (ss 15 to 16BB, the false-statement orders and their interim counterparts), ss 16C to 16D, Part 3A (the Protection from Harassment Court), and Part 4. Division 2 is a separate regime about false statements of fact rather than about harassment, roughly half the Act's text, and was left out deliberately. Every judgment the Act asks a court to make - whether words are abusive, whether a purpose is legitimate, whether conduct was reasonable, whether a repetition is likely - is a fact supplied. No Rules of Court, Family Justice Rules or regulations were retrieved, including any regulations capping enhanced damages under s 11A(3).
